request.system:
You verify one claim against evidence passages scraped from the cited sources. Judge only from the passages, never from your own knowledge.
Verdicts:
- supported: a passage states the claim's value, so a reader could confirm it from the quote alone. Equivalent wording counts ("$10 per user/month" supports "$10 per user per month").
- partial: a passage supports part of the claim, or gives a materially different qualification (a different number, a range, an older date, a different plan or product).
- unsupported: the passages are on topic but do not state the value, or they contradict it.
- no_evidence: the passages are irrelevant or empty.
A passage that only mentions a word in another sense (e.g. a product name in a feature list) does not support a claim about it.
evidence_quote MUST be copied character-for-character from one passage: the shortest span that shows the value (under 300 characters). Use null for unsupported/no_evidence unless a passage contradicts the claim, in which case quote the contradiction.
reason: one sentence. If the passage contradicts the claim, say what it actually says.
request.user:
Research question: What major changes did Tailwind CSS v4.0 introduce?
Claim: Tailwind CSS v4.0 introduced CSS‑first configuration, in which tailwind.config moves from JavaScript to CSS and design tokens are exposed as native CSS variables.
Value being checked: "CSS‑first configuration – tailwind.config moves from JavaScript to CSS and design tokens are exposed as native CSS variables"

<passage source="https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4">
[Tailwind CSS v4.0]

- New high-performance engine — where full builds are up to 5x faster, and incremental builds are over 100x faster — and measured in microseconds.
- Designed for the modern web — built on cutting-edge CSS features like cascade layers, registered custom properties with `@property`, and `color-mix()`.
- Simplified installation — fewer dependencies, zero configuration, and just a single line of code in your CSS file.
- First-party Vite plugin — tight integration for maximum performance and minimum configuration.
- Automatic content detection — all of your template files are discovered automatically, with no configuration required.
- Built-in import support — no additional tooling necessary to bundle multiple CSS files.
- CSS-first configuration — a reimagined developer experience where you customize and extend the framework directly in CSS instead of a JavaScript configuration file.
- CSS theme variables — all of your design tokens exposed as native CSS variables so you can access them anywhere.
- Dynamic utility values and variants — stop guessing what values exist in your spacing scale, or extending your configuration for things like basic data attributes.

…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0 > CSS-first configuration]

One of the biggest changes in Tailwind CSS v4.0 is the shift from configuring your project in JavaScript to configuring it in CSS.

Instead of a `tailwind.config.js` file, you can configure all of your customizations directly in the CSS file where you import Tailwind, giving you one less file to worry about in your project:

…

The new CSS-first configuration lets you do just about everything you could do in your `tailwind.config.js` file, including configuring your design tokens, defining custom utilities and variants, and more.

…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0 > CSS theme variables]

Tailwind CSS v4.0 takes all of your design tokens and makes them available as CSS variables by default, so you can reference any value you need at run-time using just CSS.
</passage>

response: {"verdict":"supported","best_source_url":"https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4","evidence_quote":"Instead of a `tailwind.config.js` file, you can configure all of your customizations directly in the CSS file where you import Tailwind, giving you one less file to worry about in your project:","reason":"The passage states that v4.0 moved configuration from a JavaScript tailwind.config.js file to the CSS file, and separately that design tokens are exposed as native CSS variables by default."}
